DNA’s secret sunscreen may have helped life survive on early Earth

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How did life emerge and survive on Earth when the planet was exposed to extreme conditions?
  • Researchers at Texas A&M University are now using advanced techniques that study how molecules interact with light to investigate a surprising clue about the evolution of DNA.
  • According to recent reports, the research was led by Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How did life emerge and survive on Earth when the planet was exposed to extreme conditions? Scientists have spent decades trying to answer this fundamental question, including how the earliest biological systems endured an environment that would have been dangerous to many living organisms today.

Researchers at Texas A&M University are now using advanced techniques that study how molecules interact with light to investigate a surprising clue about the evolution of DNA. Their findings could help explain how early genetic material survived intense ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.

According to recent reports, the research was led by Dr. Peter Rentzepis, a professor in the university's Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, along with research assistants Keyvan Khosh Abady and Negar Karpourazar. Their study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS), provides fresh insight into a longstanding mystery surrounding molecular evolution and the origins of life.

Why DNA's Evolution Has Puzzled Scientists.

One of the major changes in the evolution of genetic systems involved the transition from RNA, which is typically a single-stranded molecule, to DNA as the primary means of storing genetic information. An vital difference between the two molecules is that DNA uses a chemical building block called thymine in place of uracil, which is found in RNA.

In a recent development, this substitution has puzzled researchers for decades. Thymine is more susceptible to certain forms of ultraviolet (UV) damage, making its adoption seem like an evolutionary disadvantage. The problem would have been especially significant on early Earth, before a protective ozone layer developed and shielded the planet's surface from much of the Sun's harmful radiation.

Why would evolution favor a component that appeared to make genetic material more vulnerable under such harsh conditions? Rentzepis and his colleagues set out to investigate whether thymine might offer an advantage that had previously been overlooked.

To explore this possibility, the researchers exposed thymine and uracil to carefully controlled UV radiation intended to reproduce conditions on primordial Earth. They analyzed the molecules using biophotonics, a field that examines biological materials through their interactions with light. Their experiments employed several techniques, including absorption, fluorescence, and Raman spectroscopy.

DNA's Surprising Defense Against UV Damage.

Recent findings suggest that the results revealed an unexpected possibility. Although thymine can be vulnerable to UV radiation, it appears to favor types of molecular damage that are more readily reversed. This suggests that an notable advantage of thymine may lie not in preventing damage, but in limiting its consequences and making recovery easier.

In a recent development, "We found that thymine tends to direct UV damage into a more reversible form, suggesting that early genetic molecules may have survived intense sunlight not by avoiding damage, but by controlling it and making it easier to self-repair," noted Khosh Abady. "In that sense, thymine may have acted as a molecular sunscreen, absorbing harmful UV energy and keeping the damage confined to the genetic bases rather than allowing it to harm more vulnerable parts of the molecule.".

Industry observers note that this finding offers a possible explanation for why thymine became a fundamental component of DNA despite its apparent weakness. By concentrating UV damage in parts of the molecule where it could be more easily reversed, thymine may have helped protect the integrity of early genetic systems.

The discovery also suggests that surviving the extreme conditions of early Earth may have depended on more than simply resisting environmental threats. The ability to manage and recover from damage could have played an vital role in the evolution of the molecular systems that eventually supported life.

Fresh Possibilities for Pathogen Detection and UV Disinfection.

Beyond its implications for understanding life's beginnings, the research could have practical applications in several scientific and technological fields.

It has been revealed that the team established a fresh set of reference measurements describing how these molecules respond to light. These measurements could eventually help researchers identify harmful microorganisms more efficiently and assess the effectiveness of systems that use UV radiation to disinfect water and other materials.

"The distinct spectral signatures we measured could support applications in faster, more sensitive pathogen detection and in monitoring whether UV disinfection has effectively inactivated microorganisms, particularly in water-treatment systems," said Khosh Abady.

These potential applications demonstrate how investigating fundamental questions about molecular evolution can also provide tools for addressing modern challenges in health and environmental safety.

Could the Building Blocks of Life Have Come From Space?

With these findings in hand, Rentzepis and his team initiative to investigate an even earlier chapter in life's history. Their next goal is to understand the forces and chemical processes that brought thymine, uracil, and other essential components of primitive genetic systems together.

According to recent reports, A central question is whether these ingredients originated entirely on Earth or whether some arrived from beyond our planet. Meteorites may have delivered organic compounds that later became incorporated into the chemical systems from which life developed.

"We hope to explore whether life's chemical building blocks formed and assembled entirely on Earth or whether some were delivered to our planet from elsewhere by meteorites and later incorporated into early genetic systems," said Khosh Abady. "We are grateful to Texas A&M University and our research sponsors for supporting this work and enabling us to explore fundamental questions about life's origins.".

By examining how DNA's molecular components respond to radiation and how those components may have first assembled, the researchers hope to uncover more of the chemical history that made life on Earth possible.

  • Ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim.
  • Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Syrian who arrived in Germany as a refugee in 2015 has won a mayoral election in the southwestern German state of Baden-Württemberg.

Ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim. He won 55.41% of the votes on Sunday, beating two German candidates, Marco Strauss and Mathias Fey.

Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.

“Today, Ostelsheim sent an example for broad-mindedness and cosmopolitanism for the whole of Germany,” he noted, according to to German public broadcaster ZDF. “That’s not something that can be taken for granted in a conservative, rural area.”.

Alshebl’s first call after his victory was to his mother in Syria, who was thrilled with the news, SWR reported.

The Association of Municipalities of Baden-Württemberg said Alshebl is the first man with Syrian roots to run for and win a mayor’s office. He will start his role in June.

'You are not a refugee.' Roma refugees fleeing war in Ukraine say they are suffering discrimination and prejudice.

Ostelsheim residents have welcomed their incoming mayor. “The fairy tale has come true, and the right man has become our mayor,” Annette Keck, who lives in the village, told SWR.

Industry observers note that strauss, one of his opponents, congratulated Alshebl. “I wish you good luck and at the same time ask for support for Mr. Alshebl, for our shared Ostelsheim,” he remarked on Facebook.

It has been revealed that the state’s Integration Minister Manne Lucha remarked that Alshebl’s victory demonstrated that diversity is a natural part of Baden-Württemberg. “I would be very pleased if Ryyan Alshebl’s election encourages more people with a migration history to run for political office,” he said.

In a recent development, not everyone has been so warm to the 29-year-old. ZDF reported the Syrian received hateful comments on the campaign trail.

The young politician went from house to house, promoting his election program, and “the experiences were predominantly positive,” but there was also a minority of far-right fringe voters in Ostelsheim that did not want to accept him due to his Syrian roots, Alshebl told ZDF.

Born to a schoolteacher and agricultural engineer in Syria, Alshebl described his life as carefree until the age of 20, according to his campaign website.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, protests against the Syrian government that began in 2011 soon devolved into chaotic war. The fighting and later rise of ISIS forced 10.6 million people from home by late 2015 – about half of Syria’s pre-war population.

Alshebl faced the dilemma of being drafted for military service with the Syrian army or leaving the country, according to his website.

In a recent development, while many Syrians were displaced internally or fled to countries in the region, others like Alshebl made the dangerous journey to Europe. He was 21 years old at the time, and remarked he crossed from Turkey to the Greek island of Lesbos in a rubber dinghy.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel had implemented a brief open-door policy in 2015 that saw the country take in about 1.2 million asylum seekers in the following years, including Alshebl.

They were welcomed into British homes. Celebrating their first Christmas together, Ukrainians wonder if that hospitality will last.

The move sparked a backlash in Germany and the sudden growth of the far-right, anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the wake of summer 2015.

Once in Germany, Alshebl lived close to Ostelsheim and said at the time he felt “there is only one thing you can do: get back on your feet quickly and start investing in your own future quickly.”.

For the last seven years he worked in the administration of Althengstett town hall, in a neighboring town. He drew from his experience, he said in his campaign, and made digital access to to public administration services one of priorities. Flexible childcare and climate protections are also on his agenda.

Alshebl, who is a member of the Green Party and now has German citizenship, pledged during his campaign that once elected as mayor he would move to Ostelsheim.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft is set for Tuesday morning (Nov. 24), and you can watch the action live.

According to recent reports, an Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Tuesday (Nov. 23), during a 29-minute window that opens at 5:45 a.m. EST (1045 GMT; 7:45 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6.

According to recent reports, the launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov. 23), but that attempt was scrubbed due to a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace.

Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit, will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which at the moment consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft.

Industry observers note that amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur, suffered a problem shortly after launch.

In a recent development, ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' firm has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's Fresh Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9.

According to recent reports, vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And Latest Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test.

Industry observers note that the Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure.

The upcoming mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following releases in February, April and June of this year.

In a recent development, editor's note: This article was updated at 5:30 a.m. EST on Nov. 23 to reflect the postponement of the Ariane 6 launch following a technical problem affecting the rocket's ground support systems. It was updated again at 10:30 a.m. EST on Nov. 23 with the fresh target date of Nov. 24.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming, with limits).
  • According to recent reports, GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date.
  • An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming, with limits).

According to recent reports, GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date. Given Rockstar's history with PC ports, we originally thought gamers were in for a long wait.

An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI arrived on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19, 2026, but PC players will have to wait a while longer. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will not be available for PC gamers at launch, and no PC version has been officially revealed yet.

In a recent development, despite that, we recently got some good news: GamesBeat reports that GTA 6 will get a PC release sometime in Q1 of 2027. GamesBeat has a good track record with unannounced news like this. According to their reporting, the GTA 6 PC release window was confirmed by industry sources familiar with Rockstar's intends. They spoke with the outlet under the condition of anonymity.

Rockstar and Take-Two haven't given an official reason for skipping PC at launch, but a few factors are typically cited when publishers stagger releases this way.

Console hardware is standardized, which tends to make optimization more straightforward than building for the huge range of PC configurations. Some industry data has also indicated that consoles generate higher per-unit revenue, giving publishers an incentive to front-load console sales.

In a recent development, A more cynical take is that Take-Two could just be double-dipping, hoping fans who can't wait for the PC launch will buy the console first, then buy the PC version later. A PC Gamer poll found that 39 percent of respondents said they're fine waiting for a port rather than needing it on day one, suggesting a meaningful share of the PC audience isn't treating the delay as a dealbreaker.

However, there could be another, less financially motivated reason for all of this.

Industry observers note that speaking to YouTuber KiwiTalkz, former Rockstar producer John Ricchio explained that building for consoles first and scaling up to PC is technically easier than the reverse, since consoles have fixed, predictable hardware. According to IGN, Ricchio remarked it's simpler to start with tighter constraints and add polish later than to build a PC-first game and then try to trim it down to fit console limitations.

Without an official release date, gamers have had to speculate on the most likely launch window for a GTA 6 PC version.

If you look at several past Rockstar games, you can see that there's typically a significant amount of time between the console launch and the PC port.

Grand Theft Auto 4 was released in April 2008 and didn't reach PC's until December. Grand Theft Auto V was released in Sept. 2013, and its PC counterpart was released 19 months later in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC roughly a year after its console release.

According to recent reports, the one exception was Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition, which released simultaneously across platforms in 2021. Based on that track record, a GTA 6 PC port, if it follows the usual pattern, could be a year or more away.

It has been revealed that A report from The Verge claimed that Xbox would have exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 via its cloud gaming service at launch, a claim that was recently confirmed. The report noted that PC gamers would be able to play GTA 6 on day one, despite Rockstar's lack of news about a potential release window for a PC port. Unfortunately, Xbox Gaming's Chief Strategy Officer, Matthew Ball, shot down this report. Ball wrote on his personal X account that The Verge's coverage led to some "misreporting.".

Again, the game will be available to play on Xbox consoles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, but that service faces strict monthly limits, which will make it difficult to play through the game in a timely fashion.

Fortunately, a GamesBeat report suggests gamers may not have to wait a full year for a PC release, though it remains unconfirmed.

Russian  ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown — killed two people and wounded dozens of others, local officials noted Saturday.

The attacks come amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine, on three occasions this week, struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to the Kerch attack, as the bridge is vital for war supplies for Russian forces in the south.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Among the dead in Friday evening's double-tap strikes on Kryvyi Rih were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while several children were among the 60 wounded, the Ukrainian officials said.

Several fires broke out and damage was caused to about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram.

Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia's Defense Ministry stated a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.

Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow stated was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.

Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday.

One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.

In Russia, local officials remarked Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, said it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity.".

After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy.

NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding.

This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base. Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads.

NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a tech giant’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases.

In a recent development, the latest Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions.

The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies.

Following are a few examples of research supported through these recent awards:.

According to recent reports, an SBIR Phase II award for Opterus Research and Development Inc. supports a project focused on bringing power to the surface of the Moon and Mars by developing a modular system of rollable solar arrays. The arrays can be handled robotically, are compatible with various support structures, and work even in dusty surface conditions. The technology could be scaled up to 50 kilowatts, and it could provide a reliable power source to help both NASA and commercial space companies develop infrastructure on the Moon.

This SBIR Phase I award, led by Intelligent Fiber Optic Systems Corporation, aims to help lunar rovers perform complex tasks independently on the Moon. The firm’s 10-foot, extendable robotic arm can both “see” and has a sense of touch, combining a camera with sensors to detect and measure surface textures, contact forces, and temperature. The technology could help automate many lunar surface tasks, such as cleaning solar panels, positioning habitat structures, and collecting scientific samples from hard-to-reach locations. On Earth, the same instrumented robotic arms could be used to inspect and repair power lines, nuclear reactors, or other infrastructure in hazardous environments.

Elementium Materials Inc., selected for an SBIR Phase I award, is developing an ultra-cold-tolerant battery module for space applications and cold-climate uses on Earth. The technology can operate down to minus 76 degrees Fahrenheit without active heating, reducing the need for heaters and insulating layers to work on the Moon. With the space and mass that’s saved, NASA missions can launch other tools and science experiments, instead. This battery technology could help keep rovers, habitats, and other infrastructure running through the frigid, 14-day lunar night and potentially on Mars.

Industry observers note that A collaboration between Slate Geotechnical Consultants Inc. and the Colorado School of Mines will evaluate two approaches to preparing lunar regolith for repeated lunar landings, so that routine mission activities can have sturdy, reusable landing pads. Without such pads, the force generated by a rocket can blast out loose, gravel-like regolith from the surface, throw up dust, or create craters, potentially damaging spacecraft and nearby infrastructure. The project, supported by an STTR Phase I award, will also investigate ways to use rovers to repair and maintain future lunar landing pads.

Complete lists of the selected proposals are available on the SBIR/STTR program’s website: Phase I: 2026 NASA SBIR Appendix A Phase I 2026 NASA SBIR Appendix B Phase I 2026 NASA STTR Appendix B Phase I Phase II: 2025 NASA SBIR Phase II NASA’s SBIR/STTR program is part of the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate and is managed by NASA’s Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley.

A 194-year-old tortoise has a remarkable anti-aging secret hidden in its DNA

💡 Key Takeaways
  • At an estimated 194 years old, a giant tortoise named Jonathan has lived longer than any other known land animal alive today.
  • In a recent development, the findings suggest that Jonathan's remarkable longevity involves more than simply inheriting favorable genes.
  • In a study published in Science Advances, researchers identified 287 distinctive genetic variants associated with protection against the effects of aging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At an estimated 194 years old, a giant tortoise named Jonathan has lived longer than any other known land animal alive today. Now, scientists studying his extraordinary lifespan have uncovered genetic clues that may explain how he has remained so resilient for nearly two centuries.

In a recent development, the findings suggest that Jonathan's remarkable longevity involves more than simply inheriting favorable genes. His body also appears to have avoided some of the genetic changes that normally accumulate with age, helping preserve important biological functions.

In a study published in Science Advances, researchers identified 287 distinctive genetic variants associated with protection against the effects of aging. These variants influence several essential processes, including repairing damaged DNA, limiting inflammation, controlling insulin activity, and suppressing cancer.

According to recent reports, jonathan is an Aldabra giant tortoise (Aldabrachelys gigantea) believed to have hatched in 1832. That means he was already alive during the lifetimes of Charles Darwin and Queen Victoria. Today, he holds the distinction of being both the oldest living giant tortoise and the oldest known living land animal.

A 194-Year-Old Tortoise With Remarkably Youthful Gene Regulation.

It has been revealed that one of the most surprising discoveries came when scientists examined Jonathan's epigenome, the system of chemical markers that helps determine which genes are switched on or off. These regulatory mechanisms typically change as animals grow older, potentially disrupting notable cellular processes and contributing to age-related deterioration.

To investigate how Jonathan's biology has changed over time, the researchers compared his epigenome with those of younger giant tortoises belonging to the same species.

They found that the regulatory mechanisms associated with DNA repair and metabolism had remained remarkably stable. Despite Jonathan's advanced age, these genetic controls closely resembled those found in his much younger relatives.

The results suggest that maintaining stable gene regulation could be one of the factors helping giant tortoises withstand the biological stresses of aging for exceptionally long periods.

This research also represents the first investigation of the epigenome of a giant tortoise. The project was led by Kallel, a US nonprofit organization focused on longevity research. Its scientists believe that examining the biology of animals capable of surviving for centuries could reveal important latest insights into the mechanisms of extreme longevity.

Industry observers note that "We found that the gene regulators involved in energy production and DNA repair have remained incredibly stable in Jonathan over almost two centuries," mentioned Dr. Justin Gerlach at Peterhouse at the University of Cambridge, who was involved in the study.

He added: "There are few creatures that could tell us more about aging than the giant tortoises of the Galapagos and Seychelles islands. Working with a really old giant tortoise is such a privilege: you get a sense of the tortoise being your collaborator, not your study subject.".

Industry observers note that gerlach has spent several decades investigating giant tortoise ecology and conservation. However, this project marks his first examination of the biological mechanisms responsible for their exceptional lifespans.

Could Giant Tortoise DNA Reveal Secrets to Human Longevity?

The researchers hope Jonathan's genetic characteristics could eventually help scientists develop latest approaches to slowing age-related decline and preventing chronic diseases in humans.

By identifying the biological systems that allow certain animals to remain healthy for extraordinarily long periods, researchers may be able to uncover protective mechanisms that could inform future medical treatments.

"Nature has already solved the puzzle of aging in remarkable ways, and Jonathan's genome provides a blueprint for cellular resilience," mentioned Stephen Clark, MD, PhD, founder of Kallel and senior author of the study.

He added: "Our goal is to take these evolutionary insights and immediately translate them into practical, affordable treatments for everyday people. Aging is the greatest risk factor for nearly every chronic disease we face, and through the generosity of philanthropic partners, we can democratize access to longevity medicine.".

Although the findings provide intriguing clues about extreme longevity, translating these discoveries into treatments for humans will require further research.

Nearly Two Centuries of Life on a Remote Atlantic Island.

Jonathan has spent most of his exceptionally long life on St. Helena, a British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic Ocean. He lives on the grounds of Plantation House, the official residence of the island's governor.

He arrived on St. Helena from the Seychelles 144 years ago as a gift to the governor. Jonathan was already fully grown when he reached the island, providing further evidence of his remarkable age.

The giant tortoises native to the Galapagos and Seychelles islands are among the last surviving representatives of a group of enormous reptiles that once played dominant ecological roles across many of the world's islands.

Industry observers note that today, these extraordinary survivors offer scientists a rare opportunity to investigate how evolution has equipped certain animals to withstand the effects of time. Jonathan's unusually stable genetic regulation provides a particularly intriguing window into the biology of aging and the possibility of extending healthy life.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Aviation Administration remarked Tuesday it would pause the installation of fresh routers after problems with the technology led the agency to issue a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.

According to recent reports, tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours. It was the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news about the pause.

The FAA and Department of Transportation have said L3Harris was working to convert the communications network from copper wires to fiber optic.

Democratic members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation this week asked the FAA and the Department of Transportation for clarity on what went wrong.

"Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed," the senators wrote in a statement. "Modernization cannot come at the expense of operational safety.".

The agencies have stated they are working to figure out the root cause of the concern and have reiterated that there is no indication of a cyberattack or outside threat.

In a recent development, the senators also asked for a briefing with the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper Networks, which is making the fresh devices, by Monday. They asked the companies to lay out why the operational systems lacked sufficient redundancy and answer other questions about what led to the outage.

CNBC has reached out to L3Harris and Juniper Networks for comment.

It has been revealed that duffy on Friday called for Congress to approve $50 billion in funding for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system, more than he has previously asked for. Democratic lawmakers pushed back on the request, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Senate Commerce Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said Tuesday that he thinks there will be support for air traffic control modernization, but that the allocation should be specifically for safety upgrades.

According to recent reports, "I don't think the full $50 billion will be funded," he noted. "Some of that is not safety related, but we just discussed there, and what I expressed is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.".

In a recent development, duffy dismissed the idea that the router issue had to do with the introduction of artificial intelligence tools and remarked it was "completely unfounded" because the AI system is not in communication with the defective router. He added that the FBI is helping to investigate the root cause of the issue.

Aging equipment and a shortage of air traffic controllers have for years angered airline executives, who have complained about the cost of resulting disruptions.

— CNBC's Phil LeBeau, Leslie Josephs and Justin Papp contributed to this report.

#139093. A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way

A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1156 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, newly introduced research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors.
  • Sources indicate that the discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas.
  • Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, newly introduced research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors. The findings also raise questions about a familiar feature of the Milky Way, suggesting that part of what astronomers have long considered a spiral arm may actually be something else.

Sources indicate that the discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas. These waves squeeze the gas together, creating conditions that allow latest stars to form in a region where such intense forces usually prevent their birth.

Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.

Lead author Dr. Hillary Davis, who recently completed her PhD at the University of Sydney's School of Physics and Sydney Institute for Astronomy, said the research provides upcoming insights into the structures near the galactic center and how gas moves around them.

According to recent reports, "At its heart, star formation is a process we understand from everyday physics. Forces set matter in motion. In this case gas is compressed, and that compression can create the conditions for latest stars to be born on a massive scale," Dr. Davis mentioned.

"In most similar galaxies, star formation very commonly occurs along spiral arms. What's extraordinary is seeing this happen in a different region of our Galaxy, where shocks are usually so strong that star formation is often suppressed.".

A Hidden Star Factory at the Heart of the Milky Way.

The Milky Way belongs to a class of galaxies known as barred spiral galaxies. Unlike galaxies with only a central concentration of stars and surrounding spiral arms, these systems contain an elongated structure of stars stretching across their central region. In our galaxy, this structure is called the Galactic bar.

As the bar rotates, its gravity influences nearby gas, driving it into powerful shock fronts. These fronts compress the gas in much the same way that a shock wave compresses air.

Studying this structure from Earth is particularly difficult because we are located inside the Milky Way rather than viewing it from the outside. Large amounts of cosmic dust also block our view of the galactic center.

"The Galactic bar cannot be easily observed because of a combination of our position in the Galaxy and dust obscuring our view," Dr. Davis remarked.

"As a result, the bar's properties have been highly debated.".

Observations of other barred galaxies have shown that these shock fronts generally inhibit the formation of new stars, even in regions containing abundant gas. The intense conditions make it difficult for the gas to collapse into stars.

Recent findings suggest that however, the latest findings indicate that the Milky Way may behave differently. Although it is not the only known example, our galaxy appears to belong to a relatively small group in which substantial star formation takes place along the shock fronts of the central bar.

"We believe that the Milky Way's bar has star formation occurring along its shock front, which is uncommon for most bars in nearby galaxies," Dr. Davis remarked.

A Milky Way Spiral Arm May Not Be What It Seems.

To investigate this unusual activity, the research team compared detailed computer simulations showing how galaxies change over billions of years with astronomical observations of regions where massive stars are forming.

According to recent reports, A crucial part of the evidence came from masers, naturally occurring sources that emit highly concentrated microwave radiation. These emissions are associated with the formation of massive stars and operate on a principle similar to lasers, but at microwave wavelengths.

By examining the positions of these masers, the researchers uncovered a striking match between actual observations and the locations of shock fronts predicted by their simulations.

"We found that masers previously associated with the Norma arm closely align with the shock front predicted by our simulations," Dr. Davis mentioned. "This suggests that at least part of the so-called Norma arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a region of star formation along the leading edge of the Galactic bar.

"This raises questions about the Galaxy's spiral structure, and the bar region of the Milky Way, which needs further investigation," she said.

The possibility is significant because it suggests that some of the star formation previously attributed to the Norma spiral arm could instead be occurring along the central bar. If confirmed, this interpretation would change how astronomers understand the arrangement of stars and gas in that part of the Milky Way.

Fresh Evidence Could Redraw the Milky Way's Map.

Beyond revealing an unusual location for star birth, the research also sheds light on the physical properties of the Galactic bar itself.

Astronomers have debated the structure's length, orientation, and rotation speed for decades, partly because the Milky Way's dust and our viewing position make direct measurements so challenging.

Industry observers note that "Our findings place further constraints on the size, angle and rotation speed of this central bar," Dr. Davis said.

According to recent reports, the team's analysis indicates that the bar extends approximately 4.3 kiloparsecs, equivalent to about 14,000 light-years, outward from the galactic center along its long axis. This supports a picture of the Milky Way containing a relatively long bar that rotates slowly.

In a recent development, the results illustrate how increasingly sophisticated simulations can help scientists investigate regions of our galaxy that are difficult to observe directly. By comparing models spanning billions of years with the available astronomical evidence, researchers can narrow down the possible structures and processes shaping the Milky Way.

"By comparing a upcoming generation of large-scale computerized galaxy simulations, evolving over billions of years, against a more limited set of observations, we now have a stronger understanding of the bar and star formation processes in the Milky Way," Dr. Davis stated.

The authors reported no competing interests. Research funding came from the Australian Research Council, the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, the Swedish Research Council, the Swedish National Space Agency, the LMK Foundation and eSSENCE (Sweden).

Computing resources and data storage were provided through National Computing Infrastructure Australia, an NCRIS capability supported by the Australian Government, and LUNARC, the Centre for Scientific and Technical Computing at Lund University, Sweden.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability issues and to inspire positive action.

Originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Significant Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

Recent findings suggest that however, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Massive Five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The Newly introduced Significant 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green indicates that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on issues impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he says.

“I thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk.”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

In a recent development, in total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from Ecuador to India. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, indicates Green.

“I think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that I’ve seen put together in one book,” notes Green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing.”.

In a recent development, according to the UN, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “New Big 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, says Green.

In a recent development, as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

A chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “New Big 5.” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” says Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, noted in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

In a recent development, “I hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she mentioned.

“The Latest Major 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Booking Holdings is bringing together two of its business-to-business travel operations in a fresh division it hopes will be transformational, betting that a larger, coordinated partner platform can generate growth as artificial intelligence changes how travelers discover and book trips.

Industry observers note that the new enterprise unit, dubbed Booking Partner Division, will combine Booking.com Strategic Partnerships with Rocket Travel by Agoda, and is set to begin operating in January. Agoda CEO Omri Morgenshtern will lead the unit, which aims to help businesses such as banks, airlines and online travel companies sell trips or build branded experiences for their customers.

"We realize that if we focus our efforts both on the product side, but also on the go-to-market side, then we can potentially grow faster and serve better partners," Morgenshtern told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

He stated existing partners will find new and better products, which will also help grow the partner base.

It has been revealed that the move gives Booking a single organization to coordinate technology, travel supply and commercial expertise across business relationships. The manufacturer says partners will be able to use its global supply and technology through white-label platforms, integrated applications, branded solutions and hotel-chain rate distribution.

The portfolio includes more than 4.7 million properties, 33 million accommodation listings, more than 500 airlines and more than 200 car rental providers, according to the organization.

Competitor Expedia Group has seen notable growth by prioritizing its enterprise efforts, including a strategy debuted in 2022 to make its technology platform available to business partners looking to add travel to their own offerings.

From 2018 to 2023, Expedia’s business-to-business revenue grew at a 16% compound annual rate, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, for the division grew at a 28% rate, the firm said in 2024.

Sources indicate that in 2025, Expedia’s B2B revenue rose 18% to $4.8 billion, and its segment adjusted EBITDA increased 22% to $1.26 billion. Those figures represented about a third of Expedia’s total revenue and more than a third of its adjusted EBITDA for the full year.

Morgenshtern declined to say how much the fresh division is expected to contribute to Booking Holdings' overall revenue and profit, but he noted the opportunity for growth is immense, estimating the total addressable market at $2 trillion.

Online travel agencies have been pressured this year as investors scrutinize how AI will change the way customers search for and then book their travel.

Companies that offer lodging, experiences and other travel and leisure are grappling with how to stay visible if AI tools become the new starting point for planning and reservations.

Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro noted on the company’s earnings call Tuesday that guests already use AI to discover and initiative Disney trips, and that some are using the tools to book.

“Ultimately, we want Disney to show up in those tools,” he said, adding that Disney is exploring ways to let guests make reservations directly from them.

Booking anticipates offering partners AI capabilities that draw on the organization's existing travel know-how while minimizing token costs, it stated.

"I see a lot of AI demos," Morgenshtern remarked, drawing a distinction between a product that caters to a few customers and one that's scalable and works even when overloaded by travel emergencies. He said he's "super optimistic" about the bespoke product — a vertical agent — that Booking will offer to its partners.

#139088. Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1276 w)

Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.
  • "We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement.
  • According to recent reports, so surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.

"We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement. "Instead, we found something much more surprising.".

According to recent reports, so surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years. Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here.".

This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects.

A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity. This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across.

Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass.

Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as rapidly.

In a recent development, one of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual.

SPIRou discovers planets by measuring how much their gravity tugs on their host star. Think of a star and planet orbiting a kind of gravitational balancing point between them called a center of mass. This center of mass is usually inside the star, since the star is far more massive than the planet, but crucially not at its very center, so the star appears to wobble to and fro around the combined center of mass.

It has been revealed that the spectrometer measures this wobble in the form of a Doppler shift in the star's light that can be translated into the velocity at which the star is moving around this center of mass. Astronomers call this a 'radial velocity'. A large gas giant like Jupiter might incur a radial velocity of hundreds of meters per second, while an Earth-mass planet generates a radial velocity of tens of meters.

Yet the object that SPIRou found orbiting close to the red dwarf was creating a huge radial velocity signals of 10 miles (16 kilometers) per second. Whatever it was, it was not a planet. With the help of the eight-meter Gemini North telescope on Hawaii's Mauna Kea, Artigau's team were able to identify the mystery object as a white dwarf.

"The unusual combination of high mass and very low brightness left only one plausible explanation: it was the remnant of a dead star," stated Charles-Antoine Parent, an undergraduate student at Université Laval and a co-author of the study.

According to recent reports, white dwarfs are not exactly rare, and even finding two white dwarfs together is not unheard of: WD 0727+482 is a binary white dwarf system 37 light-years away, for example. To encounter two white dwarfs in a triple system with a regular star though is a precious find.

Industry observers note that the reason being that the masses of white dwarfs are not generally well defined. Yet their masses are not random; they are directly connected to the mass of the star that produced them.

In a recent development, thanks to the newly discovered white dwarf being separated from the red dwarf by about 4.6 astronomical units (688 million kilometers/428 million miles) – that's closer than Jupiter orbits our sun – Artigau's team were able to measure their masses to within an uncertainty of less than 1%. They found that the red dwarf has a mass 42% that of our sun and the newly discovered white dwarf has a mass 62% that of our sun. When the white dwarf was a regular star it would have had a mass 40% greater than our sun. The second more distant white dwarf orbits the pair of them.

Industry observers note that the Welopō'ai system is therefore a good system for testing our models of stellar evolution that dictate how massive a white dwarf should be. If we know the white dwarf's mass with high precision, scientists can also use that as a starting point from which to explore the extreme physics of the white dwarf's condensed matter, which is being held up and prevented from contracting any further by something called electron degeneracy pressure – the unwillingness of negatively charged electrons to crush down any further and merge with positively charged protons to form neutrons. That takes the extra gravity from a more massive star to form a neutron star.

So why should Welopō'ai not exist? The trouble is that when stars turn into red giants they really stir things up. Even if the red giant didn't expand out as far as the red dwarf, the expansion should have destabilized the red dwarf's orbit and potentially even caused it to crash into the red giant. Yet here the red dwarf is in a happily stable orbit like nothing had happened.

"That is the question driving our next observations," said Dufour. It is hoped that further, more detailed, measurements of the gravitational interactions between the three members of the Welopō'ai system will help the team disentangle the evolutionary history of the trio to better understand their orbits and how the red dwarf survived. And because they are so relatively close to us, we have the advantage of being able to make high-precision measurements.

"Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises," said Artigau. "Even when we're searching for planets, our universe often has something completely unexpected waiting for us.".

Sources indicate that the discovery of the Welopō'ai triple system is described in a paper published on Nov. 19 in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

It has been revealed that keith Cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the United Kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the University of Manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

#139086. Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work.
  • Recent findings suggest that fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road.
  • If there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work. In some cases, my favorite overall laptop doesn’t translate into the one I want to travel with. When I’m squeezed into a plane, I’ll choose maximum battery life and portability over features like a bigger screen or more ports.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road. Of the hundreds of laptops I’ve tested in my life, here are the ones I always choose to travel with.

If there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13. It’s been the best compact laptop you can buy for years, and that’s even more true in its latest incarnation. The key dimension to pay attention to on the XPS 13 is the depth, which is crucial for air travel. At 7.9 inches, it’s among the smallest laptops you can buy. Those economy-class seat-back tray tables on airplanes are only around 10 inches deep, and while that’s technically enough to accommodate even a 16-inch MacBook Pro, whether you can actually open the lid and use the laptop is another question. The XPS 13 is even smaller than the MacBook Neo, despite having a larger screen.

Sources indicate that the XPS 13 achieves this by using a 13.4-inch display (measured diagonally), compared to many of the 14-inch laptops on this list. Second, it has very narrow bezels around that screen, minimizing the device’s overall footprint. While 14-inch laptops have become more popular in recent years, that bigger display size also increases the overall footprint—and every millimeter counts when working on a plane. The XPS 13 still has enough room for your palms when typing (unless you have huge hands), and the keyboard is among my favorites to type on.

Sources indicate that the other two major advantages for travel are weight and battery life. This little laptop only weighs 2.2 pounds, a full half-pound lighter than the 13-inch MacBook Air. You might forget you have it in your backpack while traveling.

Now, the XPS 13 isn't the most powerful laptop in the world—at least not the cheaper models. The standard version comes with only 8 GB of RAM and an Intel chip with only two Performance cores. It’s good enough for basic web tasks, but for real work, you might run into limitations. You can address this by opting for the 16 GB model (which keeps the price under $1,000) or upgrading to the much more powerful Core Ultra 7 355 processor. The latter is much more expensive and comes with twice the storage, but it doesn’t add extra weight or size. Regardless of the chip you choose, the XPS 13 gets absolutely fantastic battery life. It depends on what you're doing with it, but you could easily work through a long international flight without worrying about plugging in.

If weight is your primary concern, the Asus Zenbook A14 is another contender. Despite being larger overall than the XPS 13 (with a bigger screen), the Zenbook A14 weighs 2.16 pounds—a hair lighter than the Dell. That’s seriously impressive, and I still remember how astounded I was when I first picked it up. Asus debuts its “ceraluminum” material in the chassis, which gives you the sturdiness of aluminum with the lightness of plastic. It’s not quite as rigid as metal, but it’s not as flimsy as ultra-light laptops in the past.

If you’re less worried about working on the plane and more about lugging a laptop around, the Zenbook A14 is a good choice. The Zenbook A14 has several advantages over the XPS 13 that can be helpful on the go, including built-in ports like a headphone jack, USB-A, and HDMI. If you’re working out of a remote office or presenting to a client, these can definitely come in handy. The XPS 13 only has two USB-C ports and nothing else.

Sources indicate that there are a number of different versions of the Asus Zenbook A14 floating around out there. I’d stay away from the 8 GB model Asus sells and opt for the 16 GB model instead. There’s also a newer model that uses the Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, but I don’t think it’s worth the extra $450—especially not for a laptop focused on travel.

The 13-inch MacBook Air also makes a great travel laptop. It’s relatively small, thanks to its 13.6-inch screen.

In a recent development, in terms of portability, its main advantage over the XPS 13 and Zenbook A14 is its thinness. At 0.42 inches, it’s the thinnest laptop out there—and it doesn’t stick huge rubber feet on the bottom to compensate like other laptops do, such as the Razer Blade 14. You might not think thickness matters much in a travel laptop, but if you’re squeezing stuff into a backpack, every extra millimeter matters.

Industry observers note that the MacBook Neo is also worth mentioning here. It’s not quite as thin as the MacBook Air, but because its screen is 0.4 inches smaller, it has a more compact overall footprint. Battery life is the bigger issue when taking the Neo on a trip, as it doesn’t last as long as the MacBook Air or Dell XPS 13. The 8 GB of RAM limitation doesn’t affect its use as a travel laptop much, but it's something to consider for a work laptop in general. That said, it has a very pretty screen for a laptop at this price.

Budget laptops aren’t typically known for being particularly lightweight and travel-worthy. Most of them struggle, especially with battery life. The HP OmniBook 5 might be an exception. You can usually find it on sale for under $700, even with 16 GB of RAM and an OLED display.

The OmniBook 5 isn’t quite as compact as the MacBook Neo because of its larger screen, but it is also half an inch thick and weighs only 2.8 pounds. The Snapdragon X Plus also delivers solid battery life, plenty to feel comfortable traveling with. It’s not a laptop without compromises (like the poor touchpad), but it comes with 16 GB of RAM, unlike some other laptops at this price. That’s a solid deal if you need something to travel with on a budget.

According to recent reports, good question. Tablets can make for great travel devices because of their size and ease of use. If you need a proper keyboard and touchpad—and the app support to handle a typical workday—you’re probably better off getting a laptop.

It has been revealed that the Surface Pro 12 is the two-in-one laptop I’d recommend first. It’s absolutely tiny for a computer, even though it runs the full version of Windows 11. Even with the detachable keyboard connected, it weighs only 1.8 pounds. The only real problem with bringing this on a plane is the kickstand, which adds some extra depth. It’s just small enough that it should fit while open on an airplane tray table, unlike the 13.8-inch Surface Pro model.

In a recent development, of course, that kickstand is also a huge advantage for the Surface Pro 12 if you’re using it without the keyboard. While that would make work difficult, it’s ideal for watching movies. Set this up on your tray table with some movies downloaded, and you’ll be the envy of your aisle. And when you need to get some work done in a coffee shop or at a smaller table, you’ll be happy to have access to the keyboard and touchpad—both of which are very comfortable to use. Just know that it's sold separately.

It has been revealed that the iPad Air, paired with the Magic Keyboard, avoids the Surface Pro 12’s kickstand problem. And with only an 11-inch screen, it’s perfect for use in small spaces—with or without the keyboard (note that there is also a 13-inch version). If you can accomplish all your work on an iPad, more power to ya! The iPad Air should give you everything you need, so long as you get the Magic Keyboard. If your travels involve more leisurely activities, the iPad Air is a great device for reading by the pool or for playing games.

Sources indicate that one benefit of this latest version of the iPad Air is not only its performance (thanks to the M4 chip inside) but also the front-facing camera, which has been moved to landscape for more natural-feeling video calls. Of course, you could also opt for the 11-inch iPad Pro for extra performance (and the incredible tandem OLED screen). It’s also slightly thinner and lighter, though I don't think it's worth the significant price difference.

Lastly, there’s definitely room here for laptops with 360-degree hinges—a different class of two-in-one laptops. I haven’t tested a recent Windows device with this form factor that I truly loved, but there’s no question it works well on an airplane. Just fold the screen back with the keyboard face down, and you have the perfect screen for watching movies. The Lenovo Yoga 9i 14 is a gorgeous option, though it’s incredibly expensive right now. But if you can afford it, you’ll love the 2-in-1 action combined with one of the slickest designs imaginable. The Framework Laptop 12 is also worth considering. While it’s a bit thick and heavy for a travel laptop, its smaller screen, touchscreen, and 360-degree hinge make it a good option. It’s also one of the cheaper options available, and it’s user-upgradeable.

What to Look For in a Travel Laptop.

Whether you’re packing for a trip across the world or across the state, a proper travel laptop shouldn’t be heavy or overly large. That rules out 15-inch and 16-inch laptops, which are so substantial you can’t use them on airplane tray tables or at coffee shops. But even when you narrow it down to 14-inch laptops or smaller, there are three portability factors to consider.

It has been revealed that when you’re on the go, you want a laptop that doesn’t constantly make you worry about finding an outlet. Bringing a laptop power bank can help, but the biggest factor in staying sane while traveling is a device that can stay on. Many factors affect how long a laptop can last, including CPU efficiency, battery wattage, screen brightness and resolution, and more.

Long-lasting laptops, such as the Dell XPS 13, will get you through a long flight. The processor is the main thing to look out for. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X series of chips are battery-efficient, as are Apple’s M-series chips. Intel also has some highly efficient CPUs in its most recent lineup, though you’ll need to pay close attention to the model number, as it can vary wildly depending on the specific CPU you’re using. To dig deeper, read my extensive guide on How to Buy the Right Laptop, which breaks down different CPU options.

How Large Are Airplane Tray Tables.

Recent findings suggest that the size of seat-back tray tables varies. There’s no exact size because of various factors, such as the airline, aircraft, cabin, and seat. Remember: Just because a laptop can physically fit on a tray table doesn’t mean you’ll have space to open and use it. With that in mind, here are the general averages to keep in mind. Airlines do not list tray table sizes, but you can expect one in economy to measure around 16 x 9 inches, while premium cabins will have larger tables depending on the seat.

According to recent reports, I’ve included both tablets and laptops in my recommendations, but your choice will depend on why you’re traveling with a device. If it’s for a vacation and you really only need a device to read, watch, and play on (perhaps with the occasional email check), a tablet works perfectly. Lounging with a tablet, whether on a plane or by the pool, feels much more leisurely than using a laptop. More importantly, it'll help you avoid dipping back into work mode. Whether an Android tablet, iPad, or Windows tablet, just pair it with a compatible keyboard case—and you’re good to go.

Sources indicate that however, if you’re traveling for work (or need to work while traveling), a proper laptop will be better. The one you already have may work just fine, but frequent fliers know they prefer a more compact device. And more specifically, a small laptop with a keyboard and trackpad will work better on your lap or on small desks than a tablet.

Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

Explanation: Cruising through the outer solar system, the Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant planet. Based on the images recorded during its close encounter and in the following days, this inspired composited scene covers the dim outer planet, largest moon Triton, and faint system of rings. From just beyond Neptune's orbit, the interplanetary perspective looks back toward the Sun, capturing the planet and Triton as thin sunlit crescents. Cirrus clouds and a dark band circle Neptune's south polar region, with a cloudy vortex above the pole itself. Parts of the very faint ring system along with the three bright ring arcs were first imaged by Voyager during the fly-by, though the faintest segments are modeled in this composited picture. Spanning 7.5 degrees, the background starfield is composed from sky survey data centered on the constellation Camelopardalis, corresponding to the outbound Voyager's view of the magnificent Neptunian system. Still cruising in 2026, the Voyager 2 spacecraft is now in interstellar space.Tomorrow's picture: swirling.

Grand Theft Auto VI has been out for less than a week, but there are already a whole host of tips, tricks and memes out there.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a newly introduced draft for the next EU budget.
  • Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on major tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.
  • The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a newly introduced draft for the next EU budget.

Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on major tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.

The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.

A first draft for the 2028 to 2034 budget was proposed by the EU Commission in 2025 but was criticised, especially by a group of northern European members including Germany who wanted the budget to be much smaller.

Following that criticism, the European Council President has now suggested a new draft, which is smaller by €204 billion.

But divisions among member states appear to remain, with France immediately coming out against Costa’s new draft, saying it was "deeply disappointing.".

The proposal includes a string of new "revenue channels," explicitly intended to "to keep national contributions at a reasonable level," so that member state will have to contribute less than otherwise would be the case.

The biggest splash would likely come from a tax on companies with an annual turnover from digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU and 750 million euros worldwide.

Those firms would be subject to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data," according to Costa.

Aside from the tech tax, the "balanced basket of fresh own resources" also includes taxes on tobacco products and electronic waste.

Neither the EU Commission nor European Council President Costa will have the final word on the budget. Costa's plan will now be at the centre of hours of talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.

"This is a realistic budget that addresses our fresh priorities while preserving our established policies," Costa wrote about his proposal. "I am confident that this proposal is a good basis for moving towards a final agreement.".

But an initial reaction from France suggests that any final agreement might still be some way off.

The French presidency stated the budget "falls well short ​of ‌what is needed, particularly on ‌the Common Agricultural Policy, ‌notably ​to guarantee income support for farmers.".

"As it ⁠stands, ​this proposal ​from the President ​of the European ‌Council does not ​provide ⁠a basis for an ⁠agreement.".

The EU was hoping to reach a general agreement on the budget by the end of 2026 with its formal adoption planned for 2027.
